title: The Trinity Operator Algebra

canonical_node.axiom: The Trinity has mathematical structure: F, L,  operators with specific algebra. The Persons are functionally distinct yet essentially united.
definitions: F: Father operator, source/generation, unbegotten origin.
L: Logos operator, structure/form, eternally begotten.
: Spirit operator, action/actualization, proceeds from Father (and Son).
chi: the divine essence shared by all three Persons.
Non-commutative: order of operations matters; [F, L]  0, etc.
derivation: Divine action can be analyzed into three functional operators: F, L, .
F generates content, L gives structure,  actualizes.
The operators are non-commutative because the Persons are genuinely distinct.
They share the same essence chi, so unity holds.
canonical_node.action: Formalize trinitarian distinctions using operator algebra; use non-commutativity to argue against modalism and sabellianism.
boundary: Does not claim physics proves the Trinity.
Does not claim the operators are separate beings.
Does not claim non-commutativity implies conflict.
test: Check that the three operators are irreducible to one.
Check that order of operations matters (non-commutativity).
Check that the operators share the same essence.
Check that physical analogies are used only as pointers, not proof.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a formal algebraic structure for trinitarian distinctions, enabling precise articulation against modalism and sabellianism.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the core trinitarian doctrine of three Persons in one essence.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this, the defense against modalism and sabellianism loses its formal rigor and may fall back to mere assertion.

classification.recommended_atom_action: preserve as theological model; do not treat as proven physics

overstatement_risks: Claiming the algebra is proven or necessary.
Implying physical non-commutativity validates the theology.
Overstating the precision of the operator analogy.
kill_conditions: If the operators are shown reducible to one.
If the order of operations is shown irrelevant.
If the operators are shown to be separate beings.
risk.lean_target: Formalize trinitarian distinctions without claiming empirical proof.

plain_summary: This document proposes a mathematical formalism for the Trinity using operators F, L,  to represent the Father, Son, and Spirit. It argues that their non-commutative algebra reflects genuine distinction while sharing one essence. It uses this to refute modalism and sabellianism. However, the formalism is a theological model, not a proven mathematical theorem, and should be treated as such.
